importance_ranking.reason: High visual sub-type variation — single-seater FRP cabin, multi-seater block, toilet van, and urinal block are visually distinct product classes. Buyers use the image to identify product type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Seating count, mounting type, wall material, and waste system are non-interchangeable shortlisting gates. A buyer needing a 4-seater bio-digester unit cannot substitute a 2-seater septic tank cabin; listings without these specs cannot be evaluated.

Price varies substantially across seating count, mounting type, and material — a single-seater FRP cabin and a 10-seater trailer-mounted van are not price-comparable. Indian construction buyers are price-sensitive but compare prices only after confirming spec equivalence; bulk orders are always negotiated.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall in this category — market is fragmented across regional FRP fabricators; buyers search by spec and price, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Government tender buyers and institutional purchasers evaluate manufacturer credentials, ISO certification, and installation track record during vendor selection. For construction contractors, company matters for warranty and after-sales support but ranks below spec and price in the initial shortlist.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Rental operators quote per day or per event, but all purchase listings are per piece. Multi-seater blocks are also quoted per unit (the whole block). No buyer ever questions the unit for a discrete cabin structure.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit is entirely implied — every mobile toilet is a discrete, self-contained structure sold per piece. No buyer would question whether a toilet cabin is sold per piece.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Seating count defines the product class — a 1-seater cabin and a 10-seater block are non-interchangeable and carry the largest price delta in this category.

Mounting type defines the mobility class — a skid-mounted static cabin and a trailer-mounted mobile toilet van are fundamentally different products at very different price points and cannot be substituted.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Construction site buyers need footprint dimensions (length × width × height) for space allocation planning and transport logistics; tender specifications frequently include dimensional requirements.

top_rfq_specs.reason: FRP, HDPE, and MS are supplied by different manufacturer types at different price points; a seller who only fabricates FRP units cannot fulfil an MS order, making this the primary routing spec.
Indian-pan and Western-seat configurations are non-interchangeable at the factory level; sellers need this to confirm they can supply the required configuration.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Seating count is the primary determinant of product class and price range — sellers cannot quote accurately without knowing whether the buyer needs a 1-seater cabin or a 10-seater block.
Bio-digester, septic tank, and chemical tank systems determine deployment feasibility in locations without sewage connection; sellers need this to confirm product eligibility for the buyer's site.
